title_en: Zhang Mu — Application for State Compensation
ruling_gist_en: A husband and wife were criminally prosecuted for suspected joint crimes. The seizure of the disputed funds and the subsequent execution of penalties occurred during the existence of the marital relationship between the two parties, and no actual distinction was made between their respective shares. After the husband and wife were acquitted by a retrial of the people's court, the people's court returned all the disputed funds upon the application of one party. Such act was not improper, and did not affect the substantive rights and interests of the husband and wife to dispose of the funds as joint marital property. After divorce, the other party's claim for compensation on the ground that the original return of funds infringed upon his or her individual property rights lacked legal basis, and the compensation committee of the people's court did not support it.
keywords_en: state compensation; retrial; Supreme People's Court; Beijing; Tianjin; natural person; State Compensation Law; whether the act of returning funds infringes upon individual property rights; disposition of joint marital property; dismissal of claims; wrongful criminal conviction; joint marital property; act of returning funds; marriage; divorce
full_text_en:
Zhang Mu's Application for State Compensation

【Ruling Summary】

Where a husband and wife are both subject to criminal prosecution on suspicion of jointly committing a crime, the funds involved in the case are transferred and withheld by the judicial authority and the subsequent execution of the criminal penalty occurs during the subsistence of the marital relationship between the husband and wife, and the respective shares of each party in the funds are not actually differentiated. After the criminal judgment against the husband and wife is reversed in a retrial by the people's court, and the people's court, upon application by one party, returns all of the funds involved, this act is not improper, nor does it affect the substantive rights and interests of the husband and wife to dispose of the funds as community property. After divorce, the other party's claim for compensation on the ground that the original act of returning the funds infringed upon their personal property rights lacks legal basis, and the Compensation Committee of the people's court shall not support it.

Compensation Committee of the Supreme People's Court
State Compensation Decision

(2012) Fa Wei Pei Zi No. 1

Compensation Claimant: Zhang Mu, male, Han Chinese, born in 1967, residing in Chaoyang District, Beijing.

Agent ad litem: Wang Shuren, lawyer at Beijing Junzhi Law Firm.

Compensation Obligor: Tianjin High People's Court. Address: No. 2 Changjiang Road, Nankai District, Tianjin.

Legal Representative: Li Shaoping, President of the court.

Agent ad litem: Song Chunxiang, Director of the Compensation Committee of the court.

Agent ad litem: Wang Youli, Deputy Director of the Compensation Committee of the court.

The Compensation Claimant, Zhang Mu, applied to the Compensation Committee of this Court for a compensation decision, challenging the Compensation Decision (2010) Jin Gao Fa Pei Zi No. 0001 rendered by the Tianjin High People's Court (hereinafter "Tianjin High Court") on November 30, 2011, in the case of his application for state compensation from the Tianjin High Court due to erroneous imposition of fines and confiscation of property. The Compensation Committee of this Court has lawfully tried this case, and the trial has now concluded.

Zhang Mu requested from the Compensation Committee of this Court: to quash the Compensation Decision (2010) Jin Gao Fa Pei Zi No. 0001 rendered by the Tianjin High Court, to order the Tianjin High Court to compensate him for the loss of fines in the amount of RMB 15,200,000 and the loss from confiscation of property in the amount of RMB 679,500, and to compensate him for the bank deposit interest on the aforesaid amounts for the corresponding period. His main reasons are:

1. The penalties of fines and confiscation of property imposed on Zhang Mu by the Criminal Judgment (2002) Gao Xing Zhong Zi No. 089 of the Tianjin High Court have already been executed. The Tianjin High Court's assertion that the funds were merely transferred and withheld lacks a sufficient basis and is an excuse to avoid compensation.

2. The Tianjin High Court's treatment of the fines as community property of the spouses and its return to only one of them is without legal basis. (1) Both the fines and the compensation are specific in nature. The victim who meets the circumstances specified in Article 18 of the State Compensation Law has the right to obtain compensation. Moreover, the funds confiscated and fined under the criminal judgment of the Tianjin High Court are actually the property of Zhang Mu and his holding company, so the Tianjin High Court should have returned the funds to Zhang Mu himself. (2) The agreement signed by Zhang Mu and Ma Ping in 2005, "Agreement on the Separate Ownership of Property Acquired During the Marital Relationship by Each Spouse," stipulated that without the written authorization of the other party, neither party may dispose of the other party's property. The Tianjin High Court, without Zhang Mu's authorization and without notifying Zhang Mu, returned the funds that should have been returned to Zhang Mu individually to Ma Ping (an Australian Chinese, formerly in a marital relationship with Zhang Mu). This act is manifestly improper. (3) On March 20, 2008, the Dongcheng District People's Court of Beijing rendered a judgment dissolving the marriage between Zhang Mu and Ma Ping. The judgment was served by public announcement on April 10, 2008, and took effect on November 17, 2008.

The Tianjin High Court responded to the Compensation Committee of this Court, arguing: After the Tianjin High Court rendered the Criminal Judgment (2002) Gao Xing Zhong Zi No. 089, although it transferred and withheld to the court the funds that had been frozen by the original investigative authority, after the Supreme People's Court reversed the judgment and declared the defendants not guilty, the Tianjin High Court returned the funds. Moreover, at the time of the return, Ma Ping and Zhang Mu were still in a marital relationship. Therefore, the court's act of returning the funds was not improper. Zhang Mu's request for compensation does not comply with the provisions of Article 18 of the State Compensation Law of the People's Republic of China and should be rejected. The main reasons are:

1. The relevant evidence in the original criminal case proves that the funds belonged to Ma Ping and were deposited in the name of Tianjin Xinwan Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., and have no direct connection with Zhang Mu.

2. The nature of the funds was not execution of a fine but frozen funds that should be returned to the original right holder. The original right holder, Tianjin Xinwan Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., had been dissolved. Ma Ping received the funds under the authorization of all shareholders of the company, which is unrelated to Zhang Mu.

3. Ma Ping submitted an application for the return of the deposit in April 2008, but Zhang Mu never asserted a claim to the Tianjin High Court for the return of the funds during the period from the reversal of the case in December 2007 to the actual return of the funds in November 2008.

4. When Ma Ping received the funds, she provided notarized certificates of marriage registration from the Beijing Notary Public Office, copies of the marriage certificate, and a document verification certificate from the Beijing Civil Affairs Bureau, among other materials. These materials proved and included a written commitment that the marital relationship between Ma Ping and Zhang Mu was subsisting, and that if Zhang Mu subsequently sought recovery of the same funds, Ma Ping would bear all responsibilities arising therefrom. Based on the above circumstances, the Tianjin High Court's return of the funds to Ma Ping was not improper.

The Compensation Committee of this Court finds the following facts upon trial:

In October 1999, Ma Ping and Zhang Mu became acquainted with Zhang Shuying and Zhang Shili. They agreed that Ma Ping would deposit funds into a bank designated by Zhang Shili, and Zhang Shili would pay high interest at 16.2% of the deposit amount. From October 25 to 27, 1999, Ma Ping and Zhang Mu deposited RMB 20 million into the account of Tianjin Xinwan Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter "Xinwan Company"; later renamed Tianjin Zhidi Industrial Development Co., Ltd. and then Tianjin Guanbo Industrial Development Co., Ltd.; dissolved on June 7, 2005). On December 28, 1999, and January 3, 2000, Ma Ping and Zhang Mu used U.S. dollar certificates of deposit as collateral and borrowed RMB 30.2 million from the Xisi Savings Office of the Nanlishi Road Sub-branch of the Beijing Branch of the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China under the name of personal comprehensive consumption. Ma Ping and Zhang Mu deposited this amount together with other funds, totaling RMB 35 million, into the Kaixuanmen Sub-branch of the Tianjin Heping Sub-branch of the Bank of China. Ma Ping and Zhang Mu subsequently received high-interest cash payments totaling RMB 12.72 million from Zhang Shili and others.

On December 3, 2000, Zhang Shuying and Zhang Shili were criminally detained on suspicion of fraud in negotiable instruments. Subsequently, the final criminal judgment of the people's court determined that Zhang Shuying, Zhang Shili, and others, in order to obtain huge amounts of funds, individually or in collusion with others, lured deposits into designated banks by offering high interest, obtained the reserved seal cards, business license copies, and other materials of the depositing units through bank personnel or the personnel of the depositing units, privately engraved relevant seals and stamps, fabricated false contracts, used fixed-term deposits of the depositing units as collateral, fraudulently opened bank acceptance drafts in the name of the relevant units or directly transferred funds by check, and illegally appropriated the funds for themselves. Their acts constituted the crime of fraud in negotiable instruments. The judgment accordingly imposed criminal penalties on Zhang Shuying, Zhang Shili, and others for the crime of fraud in negotiable instruments.

From December 8, 2000, to October 30, 2001, the Tianjin Public Security Bureau, during the investigation into the flow of the illicit funds from the fraud in negotiable instruments case involving Zhang Shili and Zhang Shuying, froze RMB 55 million in deposits of Xinwan Company held at the Tianjin Heping Sub-branch of the Bank of China (hereinafter "Heping Sub-branch"). On August 1, 2001, Ma Ping and Zhang Mu were placed under investigation by the Tianjin Public Security Bureau on suspicion of relending at usurious interest. On October 31, 2001, the Tianjin Public Security Bureau lifted the freeze on RMB 20 million of the RMB 55 million and returned RMB 12.72 million (for which Ma Ping has separately filed a state compensation application) to the Tianjin Branch of the Bank of China.

On December 14, 2001, the Tianjin People's Procuratorate initiated a public prosecution against Ma Ping and Zhang Mu for suspected relending at usurious interest in the Tianjin First Intermediate People's Court (hereinafter "Tianjin First Intermediate Court"). On April 30, 2002, the Tianjin First Intermediate Court rendered the Criminal Judgment (2001) Yi Zhong Xing Chu Zi No. 177, finding Ma Ping guilty of the crime of relending at usurious interest, sentencing her to six years' imprisonment, a fine of RMB 22.84 million, and deportation; finding Zhang Mu guilty of the crime of relending at usurious interest, sentencing him to three years' imprisonment, a fine of RMB 18.27 million; and ordering the confiscation of illegal gains of RMB 4.5684 million. On the same day, the Tianjin Public Security Bureau transferred the remaining RMB 7,677,100 from the unfrozen RMB 20 million to the Tianjin First Intermediate Court; the Tianjin First Intermediate Court froze the remaining RMB 24.542 million from the funds involved in the account of Xinwan Company. On November 6, 2002, the Beijing Second Intermediate People's Court (hereinafter "Beijing Second Intermediate Court"), in another case, transferred and withheld the remaining RMB 10.458 million from the same account of Xinwan Company.

Ma Ping and Zhang Mu appealed the first-instance criminal judgment. On April 14, 2004, the Tianjin High Court rendered the Criminal Judgment (2002) Gao Xing Zhong Zi No. 089, finding Ma Ping guilty of the crime of relending at usurious interest, sentencing her to six years' imprisonment, a fine of RMB 19 million, and deportation; finding Zhang Mu guilty of the crime of relending at usurious interest, sentencing him to three years' imprisonment with a three-year suspension, a fine of RMB 15.2 million; and ordering the confiscation of illegal gains of RMB 679,500 and forfeiture to the State treasury. The Tianjin High Court froze RMB 24.542 million on April 15, 2004, and in May of the same year, transferred and withheld RMB 24.542 million to the court and deposited it into a custodial account.

On July 4, 2005, the Tianjin First Intermediate Court confiscated RMB 7,677,100.

On December 14, 2007, this Court rendered the Criminal Judgment (2006) Xing Ti Zi No. 1. The judgment held that Ma Ping and Zhang Mu deposited RMB 55 million into the Kaixuanmen Sub-branch of the Tianjin Heping Sub-branch of the Bank of China, including RMB 30.2 million in bank loans, and the deposit procedures were lawful. Ma Ping and Zhang Mu, as depositors, formed a deposit relationship with the bank. The fact that Zhang Shili and others used the deposit certificates provided by bank employees, forged relevant seals and stamps, and defrauded bank credit funds could not prove that the conduct of Ma Ping and Zhang Mu was of a relending nature. The conduct of Ma Ping and Zhang Mu did not constitute a crime. Accordingly, the judgment quashed the Criminal Judgment (2001) Yi Zhong Xing Chu Zi No. 177 of the Tianjin First Intermediate Court and the Criminal Judgment (2002) Gao Xing Zhong Zi No. 089 of the Tianjin High Court, and declared Ma Ping and Zhang Mu not guilty.

In April 2008, Ma Ping submitted an application to the Tianjin High Court for the return of the funds confiscated and fined by the court. On September 23, 2008, Ma Ping submitted to the Tianjin High Court an application form signed by Ma Ping, Zhang Mu, and Ma Junchen (Ma Ping's father, former legal representative and shareholder of Xinwan Company), stating: "Pursuant to the judgment of the Supreme People's Court, the applicant requests your court to return the fines, confiscated funds, and related interest that have been executed by your court, totaling RMB 32,219,100.00 (thirty-two million two hundred nineteen thousand one hundred yuan only). The applicant will not seek any further interest on the above amounts executed by your court. The applicant will not apply for state compensation procedures and requests your court to remit the funds to the following designated bank account as soon as possible." On October 23, 2008, Ma Ping issued a letter of undertaking to the Tianjin High Court, stating: "If any shareholder of the company or my husband Zhang Mu comes to your court in the future to repeatedly seek recovery of the above funds, I undertake to bear all legal and economic responsibilities arising therefrom." At the same time, she submitted copies of the marriage certificate of Ma Ping and Zhang Mu notarized by the Beijing Notary Public Office. On November 6, 2008, the former shareholders of Xinwan Company, Ma Junchen and Song Yuanyan, issued a statement to the Tianjin High Court, stating: "The RMB 55 million deposit of Tianjin Xinwan Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. in the Kaixuanmen Sub-branch of the Tianjin Heping Sub-branch of the Bank of China was Ma Ping's own funds. It was deposited in the Bank of China by Ma Ping and Zhang Mu in the name of our company and does not belong to our company. Regarding all matters concerning this deposit, Ma Ping is hereby authorized to handle them in full." On November 12, 2008, the Beijing Civil Affairs Bureau issued a document verification certificate to the Tianjin High Court, confirming that upon checking the marriage registration records for foreigners in Beijing, there was no record of Zhang Mu and Ma Ping having registered divorce at the Marriage Registration Office of the Beijing Civil Affairs Bureau from October 29, 1998, to the date of the certificate.

On November 11 and 13, 2008, the Tianjin High Court returned RMB 24.542 million held in the court's custodial account and RMB 7,677,100 confiscated by the Tianjin First Intermediate Court, totaling RMB 32,219,100, to the account designated by Ma Ping.

It is further found that Ma Ping and Zhang Mu were originally husband and wife, having married on October 28, 1998. On March 20, 2008, the Dongcheng District People's Court of Beijing, in the divorce case filed by Zhang Mu against Ma Ping (Ma Ping did not appear in court), rendered the Civil Judgment (2007) Dong Min Chu Zi No. 04542, granting the divorce between Zhang Mu and Ma Ping. The judgment took effect on November 17, 2008, after the period for service by public announcement in the People's Court Daily expired.

On November 4, 2009, Zhang Mu applied for state compensation on the ground that the Tianjin High Court had erroneously imposed fines and confiscated property. On November 30, 2011, the Tianjin High Court rendered the Compensation Decision (2010) Jin Gao Fa Pei Zi No. 0001. The decision held that although the Tianjin High Court had transferred and withheld the frozen funds to the court after rendering the Criminal Judgment (2002) Gao Xing Zhong Zi No. 089, after the Supreme People's Court reversed the judgment and declared the defendants not guilty, the Tianjin High Court returned the funds, and at the time of the return, Ma Ping and Zhang Mu were still in a marital relationship. Therefore, Zhang Mu's reasons for requesting state compensation from the Tianjin High Court were untenable, and his request did not meet the requirements of Article 18 of the State Compensation Law. In conclusion, the Tianjin High Court decided to reject Zhang Mu's application for state compensation from the court on the grounds of erroneous fines and confiscation of property and to deny compensation.

The above facts are not disputed by Zhang Mu or the Tianjin High Court, and are supported by the Criminal Judgment (2001) Yi Zhong Xing Chu Zi No. 177 of the Tianjin First Intermediate Court, the Criminal Judgment (2002) Gao Xing Zhong Zi No. 089 of the Tianjin High Court, the Criminal Judgment (2006) Xing Ti Zi No. 1 of this Court, the Compensation Decision (2010) Jin Gao Fa Pei Zi No. 0001 of the Tianjin High Court, as well as the notarized marriage registration certificate and copies of the marriage certificate issued by the Beijing Notary Public Office, the "Document Verification Certificate" from the Beijing Civil Affairs Bureau, and the "Letter of Undertaking" written by Ma Ping, among other materials on file.

The Compensation Committee of this Court is of the opinion: The Criminal Judgment (2002) Gao Xing Zhong Zi No. 089 of the Tianjin High Court, finding Ma Ping and Zhang Mu guilty of the crime of relending at usurious interest, sentenced Ma Ping to a fine of RMB 19 million, Zhang Mu to a fine of RMB 15.2 million, and ordered the confiscation of illegal gains of RMB 679,500 and forfeiture to the State treasury. During the period when the judgment was in effect, the Tianjin High Court and the Tianjin First Intermediate Court transferred, withheld, confiscated, and held in custody the funds involved in the case previously frozen by the Tianjin Public Security Bureau, totaling RMB 32,219,100 (including interest of RMB 397,100). The court did not differentiate between the respective shares of fines and confiscated property attributable to Ma Ping and Zhang Mu in accordance with the aforesaid sentencing items, nor did it execute against any other funds of Ma Ping and Zhang Mu. Furthermore, the funds were not forfeited to the State treasury. The Criminal Judgment (2006) Xing Ti Zi No. 1 of this Court, finding that the conduct of Ma Ping and Zhang Mu did not constitute a crime, quashed the Criminal Judgment (2001) Yi Zhong Xing Chu Zi No. 177 of the Tianjin First Intermediate Court and the Criminal Judgment (2002) Gao Xing Zhong Zi No. 089 of the Tianjin High Court, and declared Ma Ping and Zhang Mu not guilty.

According to the valid criminal judgment of the people's court, the funds involved were deposited by Ma Ping and Zhang Mu in the name of Xinwan Company, and the criminal judgment did not differentiate the respective shares of Ma Ping and Zhang Mu in the property. The statement of the shareholders of Xinwan Company also confirmed that the funds involved were Ma Ping's own funds, deposited by Ma Ping and Zhang Mu in the name of Xinwan Company, and did not belong to Xinwan Company. The deposit of the funds by Ma Ping and Zhang Mu in the name of Xinwan Company, as well as the freezing, transfer, withholding, confiscation, and custodial holding of the funds by the judicial authorities, all occurred during the subsistence of the marital relationship between Ma Ping and Zhang Mu. Moreover, neither the criminal judgment nor the process of freezing, transferring, withholding, and subsequent execution of the penalty actually differentiated the respective shares of Ma Ping and Zhang Mu in the funds involved. Therefore, the above funds should be recognized as community property of the spouses. Zhang Mu's assertion that the fines and confiscated property executed against him were personal property in his name and in the name of his holding company lacks factual basis due to his failure to provide effective evidence, and the Compensation Committee of this Court does not accept it.

After the Criminal Judgment (2006) Xing Ti Zi No. 1 of this Court took effect, Ma Ping submitted to the Tianjin High Court an application form signed by Ma Ping, Zhang Mu, and Ma Junchen, along with the statement and power of attorney from the shareholders of Xinwan Company, proof of the marital relationship between Ma Ping and Zhang Mu, and other materials, applying for the return of the funds involved totaling RMB 32,219,100. The document verification certificate issued by the Beijing Civil Affairs Bureau also confirmed that at the time, Ma Ping and Zhang Mu were indeed in a marital relationship. Based on the above circumstances, the Tianjin High Court returned all of the funds to Ma Ping without notifying Zhang Mu to be present. Although this step was improper, it does not affect the substantive rights and interests of Ma Ping and Zhang Mu to dispose of the funds as community property, nor does it result in the legal consequences alleged by Zhang Mu of a substantive disposition of his personal property or failure to return it. Moreover, matters concerning how community property of the spouses should be disposed of are not within the scope of review in criminal cases or state compensation cases. If Zhang Mu believes he has rights to the funds, he may seek resolution through other legal channels. Therefore, Zhang Mu's subsequent application for the return of or compensation for a part of the funds involved lacks legal basis, and the Compensation Committee of this Court does not support it.

In summary, the funds involved in the erroneous criminal judgment of the Tianjin High Court, totaling RMB 32,219,100, have actually been fully returned. The application and reasons submitted by Zhang Mu to the Compensation Committee of this Court lack factual and legal basis and should not be supported. The Compensation Decision (2010) Jin Gao Fa Pei Zi No. 0001 of the Tianjin High Court has clear findings of fact and correctly applied the law, and should be upheld. Pursuant to Article 18, Item (2), Article 24, Paragraph 3, and Article 29 of the State Compensation Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 2 of the Interpretation (I) of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the State Compensation Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 19, Item (1) and Article 20 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on the Procedures for the Compensation Committee of the People's Court to Hear State Compensation Cases, the Compensation Committee of this Court decides as follows:

The Compensation Decision (2010) Jin Gao Fa Pei Zi No. 0001 of the Tianjin High People's Court is upheld.

This decision is a legally effective decision.

July 16, 2013
